```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(corrplot)
library(GGally)

# (a) Load the Dataset and Examine for Missing Values, Duplicates, or Outliers
# Load the data (make sure to adjust the file path)
data <- read.csv("C:\\Users\\ranak\\Downloads\\breast+cancer+wisconsin+diagnostic\\wdbc.data", header = FALSE)

# Add column names (following the provided Python column names)
colnames(data) <- c('ID', 'Diagnosis', 
                    'Radius_Mean', 'Texture_Mean', 'Perimeter_Mean', 'Area_Mean', 'Smoothness_Mean', 
                    'Compactness_Mean', 'Concavity_Mean', 'Concave_Points_Mean', 'Symmetry_Mean', 'Fractal_Dimension_Mean',
                    'Radius_SE', 'Texture_SE', 'Perimeter_SE', 'Area_SE', 'Smoothness_SE', 'Compactness_SE', 
                    'Concavity_SE', 'Concave_Points_SE', 'Symmetry_SE', 'Fractal_Dimension_SE',
                    'Radius_Worst', 'Texture_Worst', 'Perimeter_Worst', 'Area_Worst', 'Smoothness_Worst', 
                    'Compactness_Worst', 'Concavity_Worst', 'Concave_Points_Worst', 'Symmetry_Worst', 
                    'Fractal_Dimension_Worst')

# Check for missing values
anyNA(data)

# Check for duplicates based on ID
data <- data[!duplicated(data$ID), ]

# Remove ID column for analysis
data <- data %>% select(-ID)

# Convert Diagnosis to a factor
data$Diagnosis <- as.factor(data$Diagnosis)

# (b) Standardize the Dataset
# Separate Diagnosis and features
data_features <- data %>% select(-Diagnosis)
data_features <- scale(data_features) # Standardize features

# Combine back for analysis
data <- data.frame(Diagnosis = data$Diagnosis, data_features)

# (c) Provide Summary Statistics and Visualizations

# Summary statistics
summary(data)

# Histograms of each feature
data %>%
  gather(key = "Feature", value = "Value", -Diagnosis) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Value, fill = Diagnosis)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~ Feature, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal() +
  ggtitle("Distribution of Each Feature by Diagnosis")

# Correlation Heatmap for all features
corr_matrix <- cor(data_features)
corrplot(corr_matrix, method = "color", type = "upper", tl.cex = 0.8, title = "Feature Correlation Matrix")

# Box plots for feature distributions across diagnosis
data %>%
  gather(key = "Feature", value = "Value", -Diagnosis) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Diagnosis, y = Value, fill = Diagnosis)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ Feature, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal() +
  ggtitle("Box Plot of Each Feature by Diagnosis")

# Pair plot for visualizing relationships between key features
ggpairs(data, aes(color = Diagnosis, alpha = 0.5))

```

2.Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
Task (a): Perform PCA
```{r}
# Load necessary libraries for PCA
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(corrplot)
library(GGally)
library(FactoMineR) # for PCA analysis
library(factoextra) # for PCA visualization

# Perform PCA on standardized data (exclude Diagnosis column)
pca_result <- prcomp(data_features, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Calculate cumulative variance explained by each principal component
explained_variance <- summary(pca_result)$importance[3, ]

# Find the minimum number of components that explain at least 90% of variance
num_components <- min(which(cumsum(explained_variance) >= 0.90))

# Display the number of components needed to explain at least 90% of the variance
num_components

```
Task (b): Scree Plot of PCA Components
```{r}
# Plot scree plot
fviz_screeplot(pca_result, addlabels = TRUE, ylim = c(0, 50)) +
  ggtitle("Scree Plot of Principal Components")

```
Task (c): Analyze Loadings of the Top Components
```{r}
# Extract loadings (weights) of each feature on the principal components
loadings <- as.data.frame(pca_result$rotation)

# Display top loadings for the first few principal components
head(loadings[, 1:num_components])  # Adjust number of components as needed

```
Task (d): 2D Scatter Plot of Samples in Principal Component Space
```{r}
# Create a data frame with PCA scores and Diagnosis for plotting
pca_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_result$x[, 1:2])  # Select first two components
pca_scores$Diagnosis <- data$Diagnosis

# Scatter plot of samples projected onto the first two principal components
ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Diagnosis)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "2D Scatter Plot on First Two Principal Components",
       x = "Principal Component 1", y = "Principal Component 2") +
  theme_minimal()

```
 3.Factor Analysis (FA)
 Task (a): Scree Plot or Parallel Analysis for Optimal Number of Factors
```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(psych)       # For factor analysis and parallel analysis
library(GPArotation) # For rotation methods
library(tidyverse)   # For data manipulation

```

```{r}
# Parallel analysis to decide the optimal number of factors
parallel <- fa.parallel(data_features, fm = "ml", fa = "fa")
```


```{r}
# Scree plot using PCA as an approximation
scree_plot <- prcomp(data_features, scale. = TRUE)
plot(scree_plot$sdev^2, type = "b", main = "Scree Plot of Principal Components",
     xlab = "Component Number", ylab = "Eigenvalue")

```
 Task (b): Perform Factor Analysis with Optimal Number of Factors
```{r}
# Perform factor analysis with the chosen number of factors
num_factors <- 4  # Replace with the chosen number from parallel analysis or scree plot
fa_result <- fa(data_features, nfactors = num_factors, rotate = "none", fm = "ml")

```
 Task (c): Apply Rotation for Simpler Factor Structure
```{r}
# Apply varimax rotation for a simpler factor structure
fa_rotated <- fa(data_features, nfactors = num_factors, rotate = "varimax", fm = "ml")

# Alternatively, use promax if factors are expected to be correlated
fa_rotated_promax <- fa(data_features, nfactors = num_factors, rotate = "promax", fm = "ml")

```
Task (d): Describe Each Factor by Examining Factor Loadings 
1)View Factor Loadings
```{r}
# Display unrotated factor loadings
print(fa_result$loadings, cutoff = 0.3)  # Show loadings above 0.3 for clarity

# Display rotated factor loadings (varimax)
print(fa_rotated$loadings, cutoff = 0.3)

```
 2)Interpret Each Factor
### Features with high loadings (e.g., > 0.5) on the same factor likely represent related characteristics. For example, a factor with high loadings from Radius_Mean, Perimeter_Mean, and Area_Mean may signify a "size" factor of the tumor.
3)Plot Factor Loadings
```{r}
# Factor loading plot for rotated factors
fa.diagram(fa_rotated, main = "Factor Loading Diagram (Varimax Rotation)")

```
4.Two Regression Models with PCA and FA Components
 Prepare the PCA and FA Features
## Choose the top PCA components and FA factors based on variance explained or   interpretability (e.g., components or factors that together explain 90% of the variance).
##Use the PCA and FA results to create new data frames with only these selected components or factors.
Split Data into Training and Testing Sets
```{r}
# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(42)

# Define indices for training and test sets (80% train, 20% test)
train_indices <- sample(seq_len(nrow(data)), size = 0.8 * nrow(data))

# Split data based on indices
train_data <- data[train_indices, ]
test_data <- data[-train_indices, ]

```
Train Logistic Regression Model
```{r}
# Remove ID column and convert Diagnosis to binary format
data <- data %>% select(-ID)
data$Diagnosis <- ifelse(data$Diagnosis == "M", 1, 0)

# Separate features and diagnosis
data_features <- data %>% select(-Diagnosis)
data_features <- scale(data_features)  # Standardize features

# Combine Diagnosis and standardized features
data <- data.frame(Diagnosis = data$Diagnosis, data_features)
```


```{r}
# Load necessary library for PCA
library(FactoMineR)

# Perform PCA on standardized features
pca_result <- PCA(data_features, graph = FALSE)
pca_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_result$ind$coord)  # Extract PCA component scores

# Add Diagnosis to PCA scores for modeling
pca_scores$Diagnosis <- data$Diagnosis


```

```{r}
# Load necessary library for FA
library(psych)

# Decide on the number of factors
num_factors <- 5  # Replace with optimal number after performing Scree or Parallel analysis

# Perform FA and extract scores
fa_result <- fa(data_features, nfactors = num_factors, rotate = "varimax", fm = "ml", scores = "regression")
fa_scores <- as.data.frame(fa_result$scores)

# Add Diagnosis to FA scores for modeling
fa_scores$Diagnosis <- data$Diagnosis


```

```{r}
# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Define training indices
train_indices <- sample(1:nrow(data), size = 0.8 * nrow(data))

# Split PCA and FA data
train_pca <- pca_scores[train_indices, ]
test_pca <- pca_scores[-train_indices, ]

train_fa <- fa_scores[train_indices, ]
test_fa <- fa_scores[-train_indices, ]

# No further transformation needed since Diagnosis is already in binary format
str(train_pca$Diagnosis)  # Should be numeric with values 0 and 1
str(train_fa$Diagnosis)   # Should be numeric with values 0 and 1


```
```{r}
library(glmnet)
```

```{r}
# Convert data to matrix format as glmnet requires this
x_pca <- as.matrix(train_pca[, -ncol(train_pca)])  # Exclude Diagnosis column
y_pca <- train_pca$Diagnosis

x_fa <- as.matrix(train_fa[, -ncol(train_fa)])  # Exclude Diagnosis column
y_fa <- train_fa$Diagnosis

# Train Lasso-regularized logistic regression model for PCA components
pca_model_lasso <- cv.glmnet(x_pca, y_pca, family = "binomial", alpha = 1)

# Train Lasso-regularized logistic regression model for FA factors
fa_model_lasso <- cv.glmnet(x_fa, y_fa, family = "binomial", alpha = 1)


```

```{r}
# Optimal lambda for PCA model
pca_model_lasso$lambda.min

# Optimal lambda for FA model
fa_model_lasso$lambda.min

# Coefficients for PCA model
coef(pca_model_lasso, s = "lambda.min")

# Coefficients for FA model
coef(fa_model_lasso, s = "lambda.min")


```

```{r}
# Prepare test matrices (remove Diagnosis column)
x_test_pca <- as.matrix(test_pca[, -ncol(test_pca)])
x_test_fa <- as.matrix(test_fa[, -ncol(test_fa)])

# Predict probabilities on test sets
pca_pred_prob <- predict(pca_model_lasso, newx = x_test_pca, s = "lambda.min", type = "response")
fa_pred_prob <- predict(fa_model_lasso, newx = x_test_fa, s = "lambda.min", type = "response")

# Convert probabilities to binary predictions (threshold 0.5)
pca_pred <- ifelse(pca_pred_prob > 0.5, 1, 0)
fa_pred <- ifelse(fa_pred_prob > 0.5, 1, 0)

```

```{r}
library(caret)
# True labels
y_test <- test_pca$Diagnosis

# Performance metrics for PCA-based model
pca_confusion <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(pca_pred), as.factor(y_test))
pca_metrics <- data.frame(
    Accuracy = pca_confusion$overall["Accuracy"],
    Precision = pca_confusion$byClass["Pos Pred Value"],
    Recall = pca_confusion$byClass["Sensitivity"],
    F1 = 2 * (pca_confusion$byClass["Pos Pred Value"] * pca_confusion$byClass["Sensitivity"]) /
         (pca_confusion$byClass["Pos Pred Value"] + pca_confusion$byClass["Sensitivity"])
)

# Performance metrics for FA-based model
fa_confusion <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(fa_pred), as.factor(y_test))
fa_metrics <- data.frame(
    Accuracy = fa_confusion$overall["Accuracy"],
    Precision = fa_confusion$byClass["Pos Pred Value"],
    Recall = fa_confusion$byClass["Sensitivity"],
    F1 = 2 * (fa_confusion$byClass["Pos Pred Value"] * fa_confusion$byClass["Sensitivity"]) /
         (fa_confusion$byClass["Pos Pred Value"] + fa_confusion$byClass["Sensitivity"])
)

# Display performance metrics
pca_metrics
fa_metrics

```
##Comparison of PCA and FA Results and Interpretability
#Model Performance: PCA likely produced better model performance in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. PCA’s focus on variance maximization made it effective for distinguishing between malignant and benign tumors.

#Interpretability: FA produced more interpretable results, grouping features into factors that represented meaningful tumor characteristics (e.g., size, shape). PCA, while more effective for classification, was less interpretable due to its focus on variance rather than meaningful patterns in the data.

##Patterns and Characteristics Discovered in PCA and FA
#PCA: PCA highlighted key features (e.g., Radius_Mean, Texture_Mean, Concavity_Mean) that contributed the most to distinguishing tumor types. PCA showed a pattern where malignant tumors separate distinctly along the first few principal components.

#FA: FA grouped features into factors that were easier to interpret, such as size-related factors (e.g., Radius, Perimeter) and shape-related factors (e.g., Concavity, Concave_Points). FA showed that certain clusters of features (e.g., irregular shape and texture) were most relevant for identifying malignancy.

##PCA:
#Strengths: Maximizes variance, effective for dimensionality reduction, and typically leads to better performance in classification tasks.
#Limitations: Poor interpretability, as components are linear combinations of features, and it may not always capture underlying data relationships.

##FA:
#Strengths: Offers better interpretability by grouping correlated features, making it easier to understand the structure of the data.
#Limitations: May result in slightly lower performance than PCA for classification tasks, and factor selection and interpretation can be subjective.
